【参考范文 · 197 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject. Just as a towering building cannot stand firm without a solid foundation, no student can reach academic heights unless the fundamentals are first laid down. The basics are not the trivial part of learning; they are the very ground on which deeper understanding is built.
In my own experience, this truth was made vivid when I began studying programming. At first I was eager to write fancy applications and skipped the elementary concepts of variables and loops. As a result, whenever a bug appeared, I had no idea where to look, and my code collapsed completely. It was only after I went back and mastered these basics that I could finally trace errors and write reliable programs. This lesson taught me that shortcuts around the fundamentals lead nowhere.
It follows that students should never underestimate the value of the basics. Rather than rushing toward complicated tasks, we ought to devote patient effort to consolidating the fundamentals first. Only by standing on such firm ground can we climb steadily toward true mastery of any subject.

lines.en: M: Hello, doctor.
lines.zh: M：你好，医生。

lines.en: W: Hello, please take a seat. I have your test results here, and it's good news. The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues.
lines.zh: W：你好，请坐。我这里有你的检查结果，而且是个好消息。血液检查结果正常，没有任何消化系统问题的迹象。

lines.en: M: So then why do I feel so poorly all the time?
lines.zh: M：那我为什么总是感觉这么不舒服？

lines.en: W: It's probably due to overwork and stress.
lines.zh: W：这可能是过度劳累和压力造成的。

lines.en: M: No, it can't be. I've always been working hard, but I've never felt stress. Other people suffering complain about that, but I don't. It must be something else.
lines.zh: M：不，不可能。我一直都很努力地工作，但从来没有感到过压力。其他饱受压力折磨的人会抱怨这个问题，但我不会。一定是别的原因。

lines.en: W: What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it. You told me you often work long into the night, right?
lines.zh: W：你刚才描述的情况很常见。许多承受压力的人都没有意识到自己正处于压力之中。你告诉过我，你经常工作到深夜，对吧？

lines.en: M: Yes, most days in fact. But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.
lines.zh: M：对，实际上大多数日子都是这样。但我这样已经有大约20年了。

lines.en: W: That doesn't matter. You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it, and now it's catching up to you.
lines.zh: W：那并不代表什么。你可能在不知情的情况下承受了20年的压力，现在它开始影响你了。

lines.en: M: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?
lines.zh: M：可是我总是感到疲惫，晚上也睡不好，这又是怎么回事？

lines.en: W: Those are common consequences of stress. And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued. I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients, so your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects. Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month. If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.
lines.zh: W：这些都是压力带来的常见后果。如果你睡不好，当然就会感到疲劳。我会给你开一些特殊的安眠药。它们药效温和，是用天然成分制成的，所以你的胃应该能够很好地耐受，也不应产生任何负面副作用。晚餐时服用一片，一个月后再来见我。如果没有改善，我会给你开药效更强的药。

lines.en: M: Thank you, doctor.
lines.zh: M：谢谢你，医生。

lines.en: W: That's not all. You should try and work less. Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
lines.zh: W：还不止这些。你应该试着少工作一些。你有没有办法减轻自己的工作量？

lines.en: M: Um, I'd have to think about it. I'm a restaurant manager and this industry is very competitive. There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
lines.zh: M：嗯，我得考虑一下。我是一名餐厅经理，而这个行业竞争非常激烈。有很多事情需要跟进并确保掌控。

lines.en: W: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else. I'm not asking you to retire just to slow down a bit. It's for your own health.
lines.zh: W：我建议你考虑把一部分职责委派给其他人。我不是让你退休，只是让你稍微放慢节奏。这是为了你自己的健康。

lines.en: W: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams. The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player. John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25. Why did you retire so early?
lines.zh: W: 欢迎收看今天的《新闻人物》，我们的嘉宾是约翰·威廉姆斯。这个名字大家可能不太熟悉，但约翰曾经是一位备受赞誉的篮球运动员。约翰，你在年仅25岁时退役让球迷们大吃一惊。你当时为什么这么早就选择退役呢？

lines.en: M: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
lines.zh: M: 梅格，我热爱成为一名运动员，但我不喜欢成为名人。我还在上高中时就处于聚光灯下，高中一毕业就转为了职业球员，这其实是个错误。我当时是个害羞的孩子，还没做好应对所有媒体关注的准备。

lines.en: W: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career, most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary. When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.
lines.zh: W: 但在职业生涯鼎盛时期放弃数百万美元，大多数人都无法抵挡如此高薪的诱惑。当你离开赛场时，外界曾推测你是和队友产生了矛盾，甚至是有伤在身。

lines.en: M: Not at all. It was hard to quit. I was tempted to stay in the game, because I love basketball and I loved my team. As for money, I turned professional at 18. So I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it, because I had great financial advisers. I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
lines.zh: M: 完全不是这样。选择放弃确实很难。我当时也纠结过要不要留下来继续打球，因为我热爱篮球，也热爱我的球队。至于钱的问题，我18岁就转为了职业球员。因为我有优秀的理财顾问，所以我实际上已经赚了不少钱，并且存下了大部分。我知道对大多数球员来说，篮球并不是一项能打很久的职业，所以我希望趁自己还年轻转换职业。

lines.en: W: Okay, that was 20 years ago, and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. Why?
lines.zh: W: 好的，那是20年前的事了，现在你又重回大众视野。你创立了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。这是为什么呢？

lines.en: M: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem. The foundation is just the latest attempt.
lines.zh: M: 我读了大学，学习了公共卫生学，了解到肥胖流行问题的严重性，尤其是在贫困社区的儿童和青少年群体中。在过去二十年里，我一直在努力缓解这个问题。这个基金会只是我最新的尝试。

lines.en: W: The foundation uses private donations to support basketball teams for girls and boys in primary school, right?
lines.zh: W: 这个基金会利用私人捐款来资助小学的男女生篮球队，对吗？

lines.en: M: Actually, we support teams for secondary school students, too, and also have some public funding.
lines.zh: M: 实际上，我们也资助中学生的球队，而且我们也有一些公共资金。

lines.en: Kate Atkinson was born in York, England, in 1951. She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author. She studied English Literature at University in Scotland. After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American Literature. Later, she taught at the university she graduated from, and began writing short stories in 1981. She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition. Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award. The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre, and TV. She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh—the first was called Nice and the second Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.
lines.zh: 凯特·阿特金森于1951年出生于英国约克。她努力获得了作为作家的资历。她在苏格兰的一所大学学习英国文学。1974年毕业后，她攻读美国文学博士学位。后来，她在自己毕业的那所大学任教，并于1981年开始创作短篇小说。她赢得1986年《Woman's Own》短篇小说比赛后，开始为女性杂志撰稿。她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》获得了1995年英国年度图书奖。小说以约克郡为背景，后来被改编成广播剧、舞台剧和电视剧。她为爱丁堡的一家剧院创作了两部戏剧，第一部名为《Nice》，第二部名为《Abandonment》，于2000年8月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分演出。

lines.en: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on. They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humor. Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful, and generally flawed eccentrics who become credible by virtue of being so fully realized. Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners. That is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character. A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters, rather than punish their bad deeds. The humor of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.
lines.zh: 无论阿特金森创作哪一种类型的作品，她的书都触及爱与失去以及如何继续生活下去等主题。她总是以独具匠心的方式呈现这些主题，并带有一种辛辣的幽默感。她的书中往往充满古怪、有时甚至有罪过、总体上存在缺陷的特立独行者；正因为这些人物被刻画得如此完整，他们才显得可信。她的书经常被称为风俗喜剧。也就是说，这类喜剧描绘的是社会时尚圈中复杂而精致的行为规范，在那里，外表比真正的道德品质更重要。风俗喜剧往往奖赏那些聪明而诡诈的人物，而不是惩罚他们的恶行。风俗喜剧的幽默依靠语言机智和顽皮的调侃。

lines.en: Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace? Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for. When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up. You can also serve as an example to your co-workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward. Strategy consultant, Dorie Clark, explains it to us this way. "I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because frankly, circumstances change. Competitors introduce new products, economy might enter a recession, customer preferences differ over time, and more. If you shake your fist at the sky and say why can't it stay the same, that's not going to do very much good. Instead, you need to recognise when circumstances have changed, so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be. That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices."
lines.zh: 为什么说适应能力是在职场中需要培养的一项重要技能？简单来说，适应能力是雇主日益重视的一项技能。当你花时间学习一项新任务，而不是抗拒它时，你的工作效率就会提高。你还可以为那些在适应方面可能遇到困难的同事树立榜样，并帮助带领团队向前发展。战略顾问多莉·克拉克这样向我们解释：“我认为，适应能力之所以是职场中的一项重要技能，是因为坦率地说，环境会发生变化。竞争对手会推出新产品，经济可能会陷入衰退，客户偏好会随着时间而改变，等等。如果你对着天空挥拳，问为什么不能一成不变，那不会带来什么实际帮助。相反，你需要认识到环境已经发生变化，从而根据现实情况，而不是根据你希望世界呈现的样子，采取适当行动。这样一来，你就能作出更准确、更有依据且更有效的选择。”

lines.en: Also, the workplace itself has been evolving. Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork, rather than a rigid hierarchy. Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility, and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique. Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company. Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too. They can reprioritize quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something is not working. They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.
lines.zh: 此外，职场本身也一直在不断发展变化。如今的职场文化和管理方式通常以团队合作为基础，而不是建立在僵化的等级制度之上。头脑风暴要求具备创造力、灵活性和情商，是一种典型的问题解决方法。无法或不愿参与的员工，很难在公司中顺利发展。灵活变通的员工还展现出其他技能。他们能够在发生变化时迅速调整优先事项，并在某件事不起作用时提出进一步的修改建议。当遭遇挫折时，他们也能迅速重新组织起来，自信地适应新情况，而不会反应过度。

lines.en: What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine. This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfillment of expectations.
lines.zh: 是什么使人类区别于其他物种？一些哲学家认为是道德或伦理，而一些科学家断言是我们更高的认知发展水平。但我认为，主要区别在于我们渴望对抗惯常模式。这使创造具有生物学意义上的必然性，因为我们在艺术和技术中寻求的是惊喜，而不只是满足预期。

lines.en: As a result, a wild imagination has characterized the history of our species. We build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols, and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design. To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key. But who innovates?
lines.zh: 因此，狂野的想象力贯穿了我们这个物种的历史。我们建造精巧复杂的栖息地，为食物设计复杂的食谱，穿着体现时尚不断变化的服装，用繁复的标志、符号和声音进行交流，还乘坐由我们自己设计的翅膀和轮子，在不同栖息地之间往来。为了满足我们对新奇事物的渴望，创新至关重要。但谁在创新？

lines.en: Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate. But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next. The drive to create the new is a trait of being human. We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions. We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not. But where do our new ideas come from?
lines.zh: 如今，许多人，包括普通人和专家，都认为只有天才才能创新。但我认为，创新并不是只有少数人才会做的事情。创新的驱动力存在于每个人的大脑中，而由此产生的反重复之战，正是推动巨大变革的力量，使一代人与下一代人彼此不同。创造新事物的动力是人类特有的特征。我们成百上千地建立文化，以数百万计讲述新的故事。我们创造并置身于此前从未存在过的事物之中，而动物不会这样做。但我们的新思想究竟从何而来？

lines.en: According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere to great minds. From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic. They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few. However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process. We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further. This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions. And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work. The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape.
lines.zh: 许多人认为，新思想会凭空出现在伟大思想家的脑海中。从这个角度看，新思想几乎像是魔法。它们以灵感闪现的方式降临到少数人身上。然而，现实是，在人类活动的各个领域，先前的工作推动着创造过程。我们可能认为创新源于灵感或天才，但实际上，它是进一步发展他人思想的结果。这种情况发生在技术领域：一项发明会促成或启发更多发明。在艺术领域也是如此，作家、作曲家和画家会将前辈艺术家的作品运用到自己的创作中。人类大脑以先例为基础运作。我们吸收继承而来的思想，并将它们重新组合成某种新的形式。

lines.en: What is a true creator? Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing? No. Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures. Thus, humans are creators as a rule rather than as an exception.
lines.zh: 什么是真正的创造者？创造者是那个能从无到有创造出某种事物的天才吗？不是。创造者只不过是运用继承之物、吸收过去并加以改造，从而创造出未来可能性的人类。因此，人类通常都是创造者，而不是只有少数例外者。

lines.en: Many dog owners would tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset, and according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right. Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time. Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions. This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change. If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odor will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans.
lines.zh: 许多养狗的人都会告诉你，他们的狗不知怎么就能察觉到自己生病或情绪低落；而根据研究犬类认知的研究人员所说，这些宠物主人是对的。狗确实知道它们的人类伴侣正经历艰难时期。你的狗不仅能察觉你感冒了，家犬还表现出了发现细微情绪波动以及更严重身体状况的能力。这是因为狗对熟悉之人的变化极其敏感，而疾病会引起变化。例如，如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌，他的气味就会异常；即使人类自己察觉不到这种变化，狗也能闻出来，因为狗的嗅觉比人类强大得多。

lines.en: Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell. Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well. Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes.
lines.zh: 研究人员还发现，一个人的情绪可能是更严重疾病的迹象，并会触发狗的嗅觉。人类的情绪会以身体释放出的化学信号在生理上表现出来，而狗同样能够闻到这些信号。除了嗅觉之外，狗还会从人的声音中获取信息，以察觉变化。

lines.en: In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone. A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness. What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes. Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear. What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation.
lines.zh: 2014年，研究人员发现，狗的大脑中有一个区域与人类大脑中的某个区域相似，使它们能够理解说话者声音语调中的情绪线索，而不仅仅是从熟悉的词语中获取信息。一个人的声音也可能携带疾病的迹象。人们目前还不太清楚狗究竟理解这些变化到了什么程度。人类会发出许多线索，但狗是否知道其中一些线索意味着疾病，还不明确。我们认为狗表现出的关切，可能更像是它们对我们出了问题这一情况产生了更强的好奇或怀疑，而待在我们身边则是获取更多相关信息的好方法。

lines.en: Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer. But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future. For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself. Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood. Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.
lines.zh: 一些研究人员断言，狗有朝一日将帮助医生诊断疾病，因为有些狗已经展现出检测多种疾病的能力，包括糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。但这些研究人员也承认，那可能是遥远未来的事。目前的研究表明，养狗本身就能带来一系列益处。事实证明，饲养宠物狗有助于增进健康、改善情绪。狗还能帮助人放松，对于患有慢性疾病的人来说，它们尤其能带来安慰。

lines.en: Earlier this month, the think-tank called Onward published a report, "A Question of Degree", which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money. Ministers, according to Onward, should "crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students ten years after graduation", restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students, if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold. Courses like science, technology, engineering, and math, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favored.
lines.zh: 本月早些时候，名为 Onward 的智库发布了一份题为《程度问题》的报告，认为创意艺术类学位的性价比不高。Onward 认为，部长们应当“严厉整治那些在学生毕业十年后仍只能为其提供极低性价比的课程”；如果此类课程的毕业生平均收入低于学生贷款还款门槛，就应限制这些课程招收新生。对于科学、技术、工程、数学以及经济学等专业，由于其毕业生平均收入较高，则应予以优先考虑。

lines.en: The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money. At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than 25,000 pounds a year, ten years after graduation. The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would, had they simply never gone to university. This isn't really good for anyone, and it's certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
lines.zh: 这份报告为政府正在进行的一项审查提供了参考，该审查旨在研究如何改革技术教育，以及如何确保学生获得良好的性价比。乍看之下，Onward 似乎确实有道理。根据其数据，大多数创意艺术类学生在毕业十年后年收入低于25,000英镑。事实上，据称创意艺术类专业的男性学生平均收入远低于他们如果当初根本没有上大学所能获得的收入。这对任何人来说都不利，对毕业生而言尤其如此，因为他们被迫忍受一种永远无法攒下钱、永远买不起房、永远不敢指望退休的生活方式。

lines.en: Onward has identified a real problem. Creative arts graduates from top universities—like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately-educated students—have fairly good work prospects. Well, 40 percent of all graduates—regardless of their degree—are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole. Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents.
lines.zh: Onward 确实发现了一个真实存在的问题。顶尖大学的创意艺术类毕业生，例如牛津大学的毕业生，由于其中有很大一部分学生来自私立学校，因此往往拥有相当不错的就业前景。可是，所有毕业生中有40%——无论他们所学的是什么学位——在毕业五年后年收入低于25,000英镑。这表明，问题其实并不在于某些特定学生攻读某些特定学位，而在于整个经济状况。无论年轻人学了什么，除非他们足够幸运，出生在拥有成功事业的家庭，否则都很难取得进展。

lines.en: If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world. The rewards that education gives us are not measurable. They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct. An education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it. We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life. If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of "value for money", we will all be made poorer as a result.
lines.zh: 如果部长们希望让教育为年轻人带来回报，就需要把视野放在高等教育领域之外，转向更广阔的社会。教育带给我们的回报是无法衡量的。它们并不总是立刻显现出来，当然也并不总是直接的。接受教育会让你成为一个不同于未接受教育时的自己的人。我们需要从人生的角度，而不是从银行账户余额的角度，来审视教育的价值。如果我们继续让自己被“性价比”之类的说法分散注意力，最终我们所有人的生活都会因此变得更加贫乏。

passages.zh: 沙漠具有欺骗性。乍一看，它显得毫无生气、荒芜而干涸如骨。对于大多数一路轰鸣着穿越莫哈韦沙漠、准备去拉斯维加斯碰碰运气，或是前往大峡谷的路人来说，这不过是一片平坦的土地，远处有些山脉，更像是以火星为背景的电影拍摄地。然而，沙漠中充满了生命、神秘与魔力。

passages.en: The Mojave desert sees less than two inches of rain a year, and like most deserts, is a land of __(29)__ . Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to __(30)__ hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day.
passages.zh: 莫哈韦沙漠每年的降雨量不足两英寸，和大多数沙漠一样，是一片极端之地。气温变化从冰冷到酷热，不仅存在于季节之间，甚至在同一天之内也会发生。

passages.en: At the heart of this vast, 25,000-square-mile desert is Mojave National Preserve. The folks managing and working there wear the wide-brimmed(宽边的) hats that have become __(31)__ with places like Yosemite. The preserve is rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities to __(32)__ your interest, especially for anyone who loves the outdoors. For a photographer, it requires patience and __(33)__ a few spare tires to maneuver the network of unpaved "roads", but the rewards are plenty.
passages.zh: 在这片面积广达25,000平方英里的沙漠中心，是莫哈韦国家保护区。那里负责管理和工作的人员都戴着宽边帽，这种帽子已经成为约塞米蒂等地的标志。该保护区拥有丰富的历史、文化和生物多样性，也提供了无尽的机会来激发人们的兴趣，尤其适合热爱户外活动的人。对于摄影师来说，驾车穿行于由未铺设的“道路”组成的网络中，需要耐心，可能还需要准备几条备用轮胎，但所得到的回报非常丰厚。

passages.en: Photographing here requires a good, __(34)__ pair of shoes and a lot of preparation. Plenty of water, spare tires, and a full tank of gas are needed to explore this unit of the national park system, which is the third largest in the country.
passages.zh: 不过，在这里拍摄需要一双结实耐穿的鞋子和充分的准备。要探索这片国家公园系统中的区域，需要准备充足的水、备用轮胎以及加满的油箱；它是美国第三大的国家公园系统单元。

passages.en: Like all deserts, though, if you are patient, you will be rewarded, as they often reveal their secrets slowly. During my last outing, I was surprised to see how much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces, much of which remains today, giving the area a __(35)__ feel and painting a colorful background for great photographs.
passages.zh: 不过，和所有沙漠一样，只要你有耐心，就会得到回报，因为它们往往会慢慢揭开自己的秘密。上次出行时，我惊讶地发现，这片区域有很大一部分是由古老的火山和地质力量塑造而成的，其中许多痕迹至今仍然存在，赋予了这里独特的气质，也为精彩的摄影作品营造出色彩斑斓的背景。

wordbank.gloss: 恰当的；倾向于……的；易于……的
灼热的；燃烧的（作形容词时表程度极高，常修饰 hot 等）
极端；极端情况（常用复数）
充溢的；满溢的（常与 with 搭配）
同义的；紧密关联的（常与 with 搭配）

rows.text: D) flat形容词
a ___ stretch of land，冠词后名词前作定语
flat 表"平坦的、单调的"，呼应"路过者只觉无趣" 前文铺垫 it looks lifeless, barren, and bone-dry，路过者的视角下沙漠是"一片平坦无奇"的土地，flat 既符合视觉特征又含"乏味"色彩，与 "some mountains in the distance" 远景一片低平相对照。

O)uniqueunique 是褒义"独特的"，与路过者负面初印象冲突 本句站在"匆匆路过、误解沙漠"的视角，褒义词不合逻辑；unique 真正贴合的是 35 题描写沙漠真实风貌处。 M)sturdysturdy 常修饰人/物结实，不修饰 stretch of land sturdy 用来形容鞋、家具、人结实耐用，与 "一片土地" 不搭。 A)aptapt 后常跟 to/at，单独作定语少见 apt 作定语虽语法可行（恰当的），但语义上"恰当的一片土地"没说清啥；且 A 在后文"more ___ to be a setting" 句里和 to 搭配更合身，应留给那处。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— unique 是褒义，与路过者负面初印象相反。unique 词性也对、放进 "a ___ stretch of land" 句也通，但本句视角是"误解沙漠的路过者"，褒义形容词违和；忽略说话人态度色彩就会被钓走。
A) apt形容词
more ___ to be，比较级框架后形容词
be apt to do = 易于/倾向于做某事 be apt to do 是固定结构，意为"很可能/适合于……"，与 more 连用表"更像/更适合作火星电影背景"，配合 more __(27)__ to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars. 上下文极顺。
O)uniqueunique 不接 to do unique 后接 to 时表"为……所独有"（unique to X），不接 to do 不定式；且 unique 是绝对级形容词，语义上也不与 more 自然搭配。 M)sturdysturdy 不接 to do，且不修饰场景 sturdy 没有 "be sturdy to do" 的固定结构，语义也偏"结实耐用"，与"像火星电影场景"扯不上。
F) overflowing形容词
be ... with 结构，空处作表语形容词
be overflowing with 表"充满、洋溢着"，与转折语义吻合 首句说沙漠看似 lifeless, barren, and bone-dry，然后 however 转折，需要一个表"满满都是"的强对比形容词，overflowing 与 with 构成固定搭配 "be overflowing with"，正好与 life、mystery、magic 这一串积极名词配伍。
N)synonymous搭配虽对，但语义指向"等同"而非"充满" be synonymous with 意为"与……同义/紧密关联"，放进 is __(28)__ with life, mystery, and magic. 会变成"沙漠等同于生命、神秘与魔法"，语义太绝对，且后文段 31 才真正用到 synonymous，更切合那里。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— synonymous with 也成立，但语义太强、抢了 31 题的位置。synonymous 与 with 搭配看似也对，会把考生骗进"沙漠等同于生命与神秘"的过度判断；记住做选词填空要全篇预判搭配归属，把唯一性最强的搭配留给真正的位置（31 题）。
C) extremes名词
a land of ___，of 后填名词

a land of extremes = 极端反差之地 后文 Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to __(30)__ hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day. 正好解释了"极端"——温差从冰点跨到酷热，extremes 既匹配语义又是英语里常见的固定表达 "a land of extremes"。
E)fractionsfractions 指"分数/小部分"，与沙漠特征无关 "a land of fractions" 没有这种说法，也无法解释后文的温度反差，语义完全跑偏。 G)parasitesparasites 寄生虫，与沙漠语境不符 把沙漠说成"寄生虫之地"语义离奇，且后文谈的是温度而非生物，逻辑指向不对。
B) burning副词
副词修饰形容词 hot
burning hot 表"灼热"，与 freezing 形成强对比 前文是 freezing（冰冻）极端冷，空处需要与之对称的极端热表达，burning 常以 burning hot 形式强调"灼热"，呼应 29 题的 a land of extremes。
H)probablyprobably 表可能性，与温度程度无关 "freezing to probably hot" 逻辑荒谬：极端温度对比里不会说"大概热"，且 probably 也无法与 freezing 形成对称的程度感。 I)sparinglysparingly 指"节俭地"，语义完全错位 sparingly 用来修饰使用、消费等动作，放在 hot 前"节俭地热"毫无意义。
N) synonymous形容词
have become ___ with，空作表语形容词
be/become synonymous with = 成为……的代名词 宽边帽 the wide-brimmed(宽边的) hats 与优胜美地等国家公园在大众认知里已经画等号，synonymous 完美贴合 "become synonymous with places like Yosemite" 这一固定表达。
A)aptapt 不与 with 搭配 apt 常说 be apt to do/be apt at，搭配是 to 或 at，不与 with 连用，语法上首先就被排除。
L) stimulate动词
to ___ your interest，不定式后接动词原形
stimulate one's interest = 激发某人的兴趣 stimulate 是 interest 的高频搭配动词，意为"激发兴趣"，与"无尽的机会去激发你的兴趣"完全吻合，且前文 rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities 也在铺垫"种种激发兴趣的资源"。

J)sprinklesprinkle 表"撒、洒"，与 interest 不搭 sprinkle one's interest 不是英语自然表达，sprinkle 宾语多为水、糖粉、点缀物等具体物质。 K)steersteer 是"驾驶/引导"，宾语常为人、船、方向 steer your interest 虽勉强可懂，但搭配生硬；英语里"激发兴趣"的固定动词是 stimulate/arouse/spark，不会用 steer。
H) probably副词
副词修饰整句/动词性结构 a few spare tires to maneuver...
probably 表"很可能"，符合作者经验之谈的口吻 作者在分享在保护区拍照的经验：耐心是必须，备胎"很可能"也需要，probably 正好传达这种"建议但留余地"的语气。
I)sparinglysparingly 与名词 a few spare tires 语义冲突 sparingly 意为"节制地、少量地"，但句中已经用 a few 限定数量，再加 sparingly 既冗余又改变重心；语义上也与"建议多备"的语境相反。
M) sturdy形容词
a good, ___ pair of shoes 并列修饰
sturdy 形容鞋"结实耐用"，与 good 同向 沙漠拍照路况差 the network of unpaved "roads"，鞋需要"结实"才扛得住，sturdy 与 good 形成自然的双形容词修饰："一双好的、结实的鞋"。
O)uniqueunique 修饰鞋偏向"独特款式"，与实用语境不符 沙漠摄影准备讲的是耐用、防护，不是款式独特；unique 真正切题之处在 35 题描写沙漠地貌。
O) unique形容词
giving the area a ___ feel，名词前定语
unique feel = 独一无二的感觉 前文 much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces 强调这片土地由古火山与地质力量塑造，留给观者"独特"的观感，unique 与彩色摄影背景描述完美衔接。

longreading.title: 2023年12月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. "The rainy season is no longer predictable," says one. "When it is supposed to rain it doesn't, then it all comes at once." Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. "Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts," says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank's $8bn Climate Investment Funds.
passages.zh: 在肯尼亚中部的山丘上，阳光下的茶树闪烁着近乎酸橙绿的光芒，农民们对气候变化了如指掌。“雨季已经无法预测了，”一位农民说，“该下雨的时候不下，之后却一下子全下来了。”气候变化是一个将影响地球上每个人的问题。对非洲人来说，其后果尤其苦涩：其他地区能够通过燃烧煤炭和石油变得富裕，而非洲没有享受到这些好处，却将承担相当大的人类代价。“非洲只占全球温室气体排放量的2%，但预计它将成为受气候影响最严重的大陆，”负责世界银行80亿美元气候投资基金的玛法尔达·杜阿尔特说。

passages.en: B) Although there are huge uncertainties as to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity. Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5℃, heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. Farming would also be hit hard. About 40% of the land now used to grow maize(玉米) would no longer be suitable for it. Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18-22%.
passages.zh: 尽管气候变化的确切影响存在巨大的不确定性，但已有足够的认识可以表明，全球变暖是非洲繁荣面临的主要威胁之一。非洲部分地区的变暖速度已经远远快于平均水平：过去50年间，非洲南部的气温升幅约为全球升温速度的两倍。即使世界各国削减排放，使全球变暖幅度保持在1.5℃以下，非洲的热浪也会加剧，疾病会扩散到目前尚未受影响的地区。农业也将受到严重冲击。目前用于种植玉米的土地中，约有40%将不再适合种植玉米。总体而言，预计玉米产量将下降18%至22%。

passages.en: C) Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. The UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. Much of this new demand will be in Africa. Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. Self-sufficiency is not Africa's goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement.
passages.zh: 非洲尤其脆弱，部分原因在于它已经在努力养活自己；即使没有气候变化，若要满足一个人口和食欲都快速增长的社会的粮食需求，非洲也必须大幅提高产量和生产率。联合国粮食及农业组织估计，到2050年，全球粮食产量必须比2009年的水平提高约70%，才能满足人口数量和食欲不断增长所带来的需求。新增需求中有很大一部分将来自非洲。然而，非洲目前每年进口价值约500亿美元的食品，预计未来五年这一数字将增加一倍以上。自给自足并不是非洲的目标，但它进口食品所花的钱多于购买资本货物所花的钱，这表明其仍有改进空间。

passages.en: D) Finding out why is not hard. Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. More than half of Africa's people make their living from farming. Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. But in many places there is no spare land to farm. Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America.
passages.zh: 要弄清原因并不难。大多数农场规模很小，靠人工耕作，并且依赖降雨。非洲一半以上的人口以务农为生。尽管过去几十年间，非洲的粮食总产量有所增加，但这主要是因为从事农业的人更多了，耕种的土地也更多了。然而，许多地方已经没有多余的土地可供耕种。卢旺达的地块小得惊人，美国一个普通农场的面积可以容纳250个这样的地块。尽管过去30年间，非洲每名农业劳动者的产出提高了超过一半，但这仍远远落后于亚洲产出提高2.5倍的水平。非洲的玉米单产通常不到每公顷两吨，只有美国水平的五分之一。

passages.en: E) The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics—despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. "They can't even feed their families," says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. "Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years."
passages.zh: 非洲农民的低生产率反映在国民经济统计数据中：尽管农业吸纳了如此多的劳动力，但其创造的国内生产总值仅占15%。“他们甚至养活不了自己的家人，”负责农业事务的非洲开发银行副行长詹妮弗·布兰克说。“非洲许多地区的农业生产率已经有100年没有提高了。”

passages.en: F) One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. Ghana taxed cocoa(可可粉) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. The results can be impressive. Improved varieties of sorghum(高梁), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety. Infrastructure is important. A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes.
passages.zh: 其中一个原因是，在独立后的最初几十年里，许多非洲政府专注于经济工业化，忽视了农业。另一些政府则通过压低国营垄断企业支付给农民的作物价格来损害农业，以便用廉价食品补贴城市工人。加纳对可可出口征收了过高的税，导致20世纪60年代至80年代间可可产量减少了一半，尽管同期全球可可价格大幅上涨。然而，在过去大约20年里，政府和捐助者开始重新把农业视为一种为每年进入劳动力市场的1300万年轻人提供就业的途径。许多工作重点放在推动小农使用化肥，以及更重要的优良种子上。成效可能十分显著。例如，改良品种的高粱产量可以比普通品种高出40%。基础设施也很重要。世界银行在埃塞俄比亚实施的一项灌溉项目帮助农民将马铃薯收成从每公顷约8吨提高到35吨。

passages.en: G) Better techniques help, too. Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same.
passages.zh: 更好的技术也会有所帮助。肯尼亚的小型咖啡种植户只需遵循几条关于照料咖啡树的简单指导，例如只保留三根枝干、剪去其余枝干，就能将收入提高40%。他们的许多邻居并不听从这些建议，因为这似乎违背直觉。他们说，枝干越多，咖啡豆应该就越多。然而，在看到听从建议的人连续一两个季节获得更大的收成后，许多人也开始照做。

passages.en: H) One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O'Keeffe, who runs its Africa business.
passages.zh: 传播知识的一种方式，是将农场与大型农产品采购商联系起来。当英国饮料巨头帝亚吉欧在肯尼亚西部建造一家啤酒厂时，它希望利用当地作物酿造一种价格足够低廉、能够与非法家庭酿酒竞争的啤酒。该公司把农民组织起来，改善供应链，帮助他们获得种子和化肥，随后同意收购他们的谷物。如今，它为约1.7万名农民提供了市场。负责其非洲业务的约翰·奥基夫说，五年来，该公司在整个地区对当地原材料的使用比例已经翻了一番，达到约80%。

passages.en: I) An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers. Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. Everything went wrong. The crop was attacked by pests. "Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital," he says. Mr Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people. The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields.
passages.zh: 一个更为重要的变化，是从传统农业转向建立能够将技术和投资以有利可图的方式带给小农户的企业。年轻的肯尼亚人泰塔·恩盖蒂奇当时正在学习工程学，想挣一点外快。他东拼西凑了2万肯尼亚先令（约合200美元）种植西红柿。一切都出了问题。作物遭到了害虫侵袭。“后来，一场大洪水吞没了我们所有的本金，”他说。恩盖蒂奇没有放弃，而是开始研究购买温室，以保护作物免受虫害和雨水侵袭。最便宜的温室每座也要2500多美元，于是他自行设计了一种，价格只有一半。很快，邻近的农民开始向他下订单。如今，他的公司Illuminum Greenhouses已经售出1400多座温室，为约6000人提供了生计。该公司的业务并不止于此；它还供应化肥、高质量幼苗和能够提高产量的智能传感器。

passages.en: J) Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. Because such a large share of Africa's population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure.
passages.zh: Illuminum的成功表明，技术甚至能够帮助小型农场提高生产率。由于非洲有如此大比例的人口依靠农业谋生，即使生产率只有小幅提升，也能增加数百万人的收入。但从长远来看，小规模农业能够发挥的作用终究有限，尤其是在气候变化和人口压力面前。

passages.en: K) "If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education," says Mr Ngetich. "Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there." Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities.
passages.zh: “如果我们真的想让人们摆脱贫困，就必须资助那些能让他们每月至少获得100美元收入的项目，这样他们才能支付医疗和教育费用，”恩盖蒂奇先生说。“那些通过种植豆类或玉米每月只让他们多赚2美元的项目，不可能把他们带到那个水平。”要实现如此大幅度的提升，就需要在工厂和城市中提供更好的工作。

statements.en: It is said that agricultural productivity in many African countries has remained low for a century.
statements.zh: 据说许多非洲国家的农业生产率一个世纪以来一直很低。

analysis.锚点: 一百年未提升的农业生产率
analysis.定位: E 段 Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years. 非洲许多地方的农业生产率已经一百年没有改善了。
analysis.改写: agricultural productivity in many African countries has remained low for a century↔Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years 数字单位换写 + 否定改善 = 维持低位
analysis.辨邻: D D 段 output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa 给的时间是 30 年、方向是「提升过半」，与题干 remained low for a century 的「停滞一百年」结论完全相反，属于只覆盖局部 + 方向相反，不是源头段。 output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia

statements.en: Building connections between farms and major purchasers of their produce can promote African farmers' use of advanced farming techniques.
statements.zh: 在农场与其农产品的主要购买者之间建立联系可以促进非洲农民使用先进的农业技术。

analysis.锚点: 把农场连到大买家以推广技术
analysis.定位: H 段 One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. 传播知识的一种方式，是把农场与他们农产品的大买家连起来。
analysis.改写: Building connections between farms and major purchasers of their produce↔link farms to big buyers of their harvests 建立连接 = link；大买家 = big buyers；农产品 = harvests can promote African farmers' use of advanced farming techniques↔One way of spreading knowledge 传播知识即让农民用上先进做法
analysis.辨邻: F F 段重心在 getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds，讲的是「输入端」做法，没有「把农场连到大买家」这件事，与题干 Building connections between farms and major purchasers 的渠道连接路径不同。 Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds G G 段 Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice 走的是「邻里看效果再跟」的路径，与 Building connections between farms and major purchasers 的「连到买家」机制不同。 Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes

statements.en: Parts of Africa are getting warmer much faster than the average, with southern Africa witnessing roughly twice the global warming rate over the last half century.
statements.zh: 非洲部分地区的气温上升速度远快于平均水平,南部非洲在过去半个世纪见证了大约两倍于全球的变暖速度。

analysis.锚点: 南部非洲约两倍全球升温速度
analysis.定位: B 段 Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. 非洲部分地区已经在以远高于平均的速度变暖：过去 50 年里，南部非洲的气温升幅约为全球升温速率的两倍。
analysis.改写: southern Africa witnessing roughly twice the global warming rate↔temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate roughly = about，witness 等价于 have increased by 的概括说法 over the last half century↔over the past 50 years half century = 50 years Parts of Africa are getting warmer much faster than the average↔Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average continent = Africa 上下位换名；getting warmer = warming

statements.en: Improved farming practices have enabled Kenyan farmers to increase farm produce remarkably.
statements.zh: 改进的农业实践使肯尼亚农民能够显著增加农产品产量。

analysis.锚点: 改良耕作法显著提高肯尼亚农产量
analysis.定位: G 段 Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. 肯尼亚的小咖啡农只要遵循几条简单的护树建议——比如把茎全部修剪到只剩三根——就能把收入提高 40%。
analysis.改写: Improved farming practices↔a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes 上位词 farming practices 覆盖下位的 simple guidelines Kenyan farmers↔Small coffee farmers in Kenya Kenyan farmers 与 farmers in Kenya 等价 increase farm produce remarkably↔increase their incomes by 40% 40% 即 remarkably；produce 与 incomes 通过因果换皮
analysis.辨邻: F F 段 Improved varieties of sorghum 与 from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes 讲的是高粱与马铃薯增产，不是肯尼亚咖啡农剪枝的故事，主体不同。 Improved varieties of sorghum, for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety H H 段 link farms to big buyers of their harvests 走的是渠道型推广，不是题干 Improved farming practices 的耕作做法改良。 When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya

statements.en: Africa is especially susceptible to the effects of global warming partly because it has difficulty feeding its increasing population even without climate change.
statements.zh: 非洲特别容易受到全球变暖影响,部分原因是即使没有气候变化,它也难以养活不断增长的人口。

analysis.锚点: 气候变化叠加人口增长的双重脆弱
analysis.定位: C 段 Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. 非洲格外脆弱，部分原因是它本就难以养活自己，而且即便没有气候变化，它也得大幅提高产量和生产率，才能喂饱一个快速增长的人口。
analysis.改写: especially susceptible to the effects of global warming↔particularly vulnerable especially = particularly；susceptible = vulnerable has difficulty feeding its increasing population↔struggling to feed itself has difficulty doing = struggling to do；fast-growing 同义 increasing even without climate change↔even without climate change 短语原样复现
analysis.辨邻: B B 段 About 40% of the land now used to grow maize would no longer be suitable for it 给的是气候导致的种植带变化，而题干 has difficulty feeding its increasing population even without climate change 要的是「即使没气候变化也喂不饱」的人口端理由，方向不同。 Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5℃, heat-waves would intensify in Africa

statements.en: The use of fertiliser and improved seeds can help Africa's small farmers impressively increase crop yields.
statements.zh: 化肥和改良种子的使用可以帮助非洲小农户大幅提高作物产量。

analysis.锚点: 化肥与改良种子帮小农大幅增产
analysis.定位: F 段 Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. （重新重视农业的）重点很大程度上落在让小农使用化肥，以及更重要的——使用更好的种子上。
analysis.改写: The use of fertiliser and improved seeds↔getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds fertiliser 原样 + improved seeds = better seeds can help Africa's small farmers impressively increase crop yields↔The results can be impressive impressively 与 impressive 同根同义
analysis.辨邻: G G 段 trimming all but three of their stems 走的是修剪指南，不是题干 The use of fertiliser and improved seeds 要的两类输入。 by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems

statements.en: It has proved even more important to shift from traditional farming to setting up businesses that can bring technology and investment to small farmers in Africa.
statements.zh: 事实证明,从传统农业转向建立能够为非洲小农户带来技术和投资的企业更为重要。

analysis.锚点: 从传统耕作转向科技+投资的商业模式
analysis.定位: I 段 An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers. 一个更重要的变化是：从传统耕作转向建立那些能把技术与投资带给小农、且能赚钱的企业。
analysis.改写: shift from traditional farming to setting up businesses↔the move from traditional farming to building businesses shift = move；setting up = building bring technology and investment to small farmers↔profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers 除 profitably 外短语逐词一致 It has proved even more important↔An even more important change 「更重要」整体平移
analysis.辨邻: J J 段 Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive 是对 I 段案例的提炼，并不重新陈述「从传统耕作转向建立企业」这件事；题干 shift from traditional farming to setting up businesses 的源头是 I 段那句首提的转型断言。 Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive

statements.en: Everyone in the world will have to bear the consequences of climate change, especially Africans.
statements.zh: 世界上每个人都将承受气候变化的后果,尤其是非洲人。

analysis.锚点: 全人类共担、非洲尤其要承受气候后果
analysis.定位: A 段 Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter. 气候变化是一个会影响地球上每个人的议题，但对非洲人来说，其后果将尤其苦涩。
analysis.改写: Everyone in the world will have to bear the consequences of climate change↔Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet everyone in the world = everyone on the planet；bear consequences = be affected especially Africans↔For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter especially = particularly（程度副词同义）
analysis.辨邻: B B 段 global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity 是具体威胁论证，与题干 Everyone in the world will have to bear the consequences 的「全体共担」总论调性不对位。 global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity

statements.en: Improvement in farm output per worker in Africa falls far short of that in Asia.
statements.zh: 非洲每个工人的农业产出改善远远落后于亚洲。

analysis.锚点: 非洲人均产出提升远落后于亚洲
analysis.定位: D 段 And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. 尽管过去 30 年里非洲的人均产出提升了一半以上，这仍远落后于亚洲的 2.5 倍提升。
analysis.改写: Improvement in farm output per worker in Africa↔output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa 动词句 → 名词化短语 falls far short of that in Asia↔far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia fall far short of = far behind
analysis.辨邻: E E 段 Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years 没有提到亚洲，与题干 falls far short of that in Asia 中作为对比标杆的亚洲缺失，不是源头段。 Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years

statements.en: In the long term, the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited, especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population.
statements.zh: 从长远来看,非洲小型农场提高生产力的潜力相当有限,特别是由于气候变暖和人口增长。

analysis.锚点: 长期看小农增产潜力有限
analysis.定位: J 段 But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure. 但从更长远看，小规模农业能走的也就这么远，尤其是面对气候变化和人口压力的时候。
analysis.改写: In the long term, the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited↔over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far long term = longer run；quite limited = can go only so far especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population↔especially in the face of climate change and population pressure owing to = in the face of；warming climate ≈ climate change；growing population ≈ population pressure
analysis.辨邻: I I 段 Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people 给的是「小农通过科技获得收益」的正面案例，与题干 the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited 的「潜力有限」断言方向相反，是 42 题的归属段而非本题。 An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers K K 段 Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there 给的是收入门槛论证，没有「长期看 + 气候变化 + 人口」这套与题干 especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population 完全对位的双因表述。 Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities

reading1.title: 2023年12月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.
passages.zh: 近几十年来，共和党取得的一项巨大成功，就是坚持不懈地传播一个关于经济增长的简单公式：减税。

passages.en: The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
passages.zh: 这个公式并不奏效，但这并未影响它的受欢迎程度。尽管减税狂热吸引了许多批评者，却没有明显的替代方案。

passages.en: Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.
passages.zh: 民主党政治人物往往以帮助那些被经济增长落在后面的人为竞选主张。当民主党人确实谈到促进经济增长时，他们听起来常常像共和党人。

passages.en: This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages.
passages.zh: 这不仅是民主党面临的政治问题，也是美国面临的经济问题。美国需要对经济增长的驱动因素有一种更好的阐释。近几十年令人痛苦的教训指向了一个有希望的候选因素：更高的工资。

passages.en: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks.
passages.zh: 提高美国工人的工资应当成为经济政策制定者的优先事项。如果少关注国内生产总值（GDP）增长的季度更新，转而关注工人工资收入的增长，我们所有人的境况都会更好。

passages.en: Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.
passages.zh: 暂且把支持提高工资的那个耳熟能详的理由放在一边：公平。这里的论点是，更高的工资能够为经济增长的引擎提供动力。

passages.en: Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too.
passages.zh: 关于提高工资所带来益处的最著名例证，或许就是这样一个故事：1914年，亨利·福特决定给福特T型车装配线上的工人每天5美元的工资。他这样做是为了提高产量——他支付高于常规的工资，以维持一支可靠的劳动力队伍。意想不到的好处是，福特工厂的工人也成了福特汽车的顾客。

passages.en: The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.
passages.zh: 同样的逻辑至今仍然成立：消费推动着美国经济，而工资更高的工人能够进行更多消费。

passages.en: Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces.
passages.zh: 主流经济学家坚持认为，不可能人为安排工资持续上涨，因为薪酬水平反映了市场力量无误的判断。

passages.en: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.
passages.zh: 传统观念认为，生产率增长是提高工资的唯一途径。从这一角度看，争取提高工资的努力会适得其反。最低工资法会导致失业率上升，因为工资总额是有限的，如果一些人得到更多，其他人就会一无所获。

passages.en: It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.
passages.zh: 正是在这种世界观的背景下，认为减税能够带来繁荣的观点开始流行。富人会进行投资，生产率会提高，工资会随之上涨。

passages.en: In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
passages.zh: 在现实世界中，事情更加复杂。工资受到雇主与工人之间拉锯的影响，而雇主一直占据上风。一个明确的证据是，大约自1970年以来，生产率增长与工资增长之间的差距不断扩大。生产率已经增长了一倍多，而工资却远远落后。

passages.en: A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote(矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.
passages.zh: 关注工资增长，将成为对减税具有神奇力量这一信念所具备的诱人简洁性的一剂矫正药。

questions.stem: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective?
questions.stem_zh: 为什么减税方案虽然无效却依然流行?

options.text: Its critics' voice has not been heard throughout the country.
options.zh: 批评者的声音未能在全国范围内得到倾听。

options.text: There seem to be no other options available to replace it.
options.zh: 似乎没有其他可用的选项来取代它。

options.text: The cult of tax cuts has been relentlessly propagated by all policymakers.
options.zh: 减税崇拜已被所有政策制定者不懈地宣传。

options.text: There appears to be a misunderstanding of the formula among the public.
options.zh: 公众似乎对该方案存在误解。

questions.判型: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective? 用 Why 直接问原因，是要回到原文找一句明确解释。
questions.拆句: 主句 Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular 加状语从句 though ineffective——though 后省略了 it is，完整是 though it is ineffective；六级常用 though 引出让步状语，识别它是看懂题干逻辑的关键。
questions.定位: P2 And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals. 尽管对减税的崇拜招致了许多批评，但它（在政策市场上）没有明显的替代品。

locate.en: And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
locate.zh: 尽管对减税的崇拜招致了许多批评，但它（在政策市场上）没有明显的替代品。

option_analysis.note: 原文只说 the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics——招致很多批评，没有说这些批评"未被全国听见"。
B 项是 it lacks for obvious rivals 的同义重写，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.opt: There seem to be no other options available to replace it.

option_analysis.note: 原文 One of the great successes of the Republican Party 明确只是共和党在传播，选项扩大为 all policymakers（所有政策制定者）。
原文只说该公式 doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity，并未说大众"误解"了这个公式。

questions.stem: What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.?
questions.stem_zh: 作者认为推动美国经济增长更有效的措施是什么?

options.text: Aiding people left behind by economic growth.
options.zh: 帮助那些在经济增长中被落下的人。

options.text: Prioritizing the growth of the nation's GDP.
options.zh: 优先考虑国家GDP的增长。

options.text: Increasing the compensation for labor.
options.zh: 增加劳动报酬。

options.text: Introducing even more extensive tax cuts.
options.zh: 引入更大规模的减税。

questions.判型: What does the author think is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.? 直接问作者认为有效的措施，原文必有一句明确给出。
questions.拆句: 主句 What does the author think，think 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 is a more effective measure for driving economic growth in the U.S.；六级常考插入语式的 author think，识别它后面才是真正提问的内容。
questions.定位: P5 Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. 提高美国工人的工资，应当是经济政策制定者的首要任务。

locate.en: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers.
locate.zh: 提高美国工人的工资，应当是经济政策制定者的首要任务。

option_analysis.note: Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. 这是作者描述民主党的做法，紧接着 P4 就把它否定为"政治问题"。
We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP)——作者明确说应少关注 GDP 增长。
C 项是 Raising the wages of American workers 的逐字同义改写，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.orig: Raising the wages of American workers

option_analysis.note: 全文要驳斥的就是减税公式（tax cuts），作者不可能反过来主张更大规模减税。

questions.stem: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?
questions.stem_zh: 作者观点背后的逻辑是什么?

options.text: The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy.
options.zh: 工人薪资的增长最终会推动国家经济。

options.text: Paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce attracts more customers.
options.zh: 支付溢价以维持可靠的劳动力会吸引更多顾客。

options.text: Consumption stimulates the desire for higher wages.
options.zh: 消费刺激了对更高工资的渴望。

options.text: Familiar arguments for higher wages are outdated.
options.zh: 关于提高工资的常见论据已经过时。

questions.判型: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint? 用 What 直接问支撑作者观点的逻辑机制，原文应有明确陈述。
questions.拆句: What is the logic underlying the author's viewpoint?——underlying 是现在分词作后置定语，修饰 logic，等于 that underlies；六级阅读高频，看到 -ing 后置定语要意识到它修饰前面那个名词。
questions.定位: P8 Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more. 消费驱动着美国经济，而薪酬越高的工人能消费得越多。

locate.en: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.
locate.zh: 消费驱动着美国经济，而薪酬越高的工人能消费得越多。

option_analysis.note: A 项用 ultimately 把 P8 的两句话压成一句因果，与预判的"加薪→消费→经济增长"完全一致。

pairs.orig: workers who are paid more can spend more
pairs.opt: The growth of workers' paychecks ultimately boosts the nation's economy.

option_analysis.note: He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. 是福特出于产能目的支付溢价；The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. 中"工人变顾客"是意外结果，并非"支付溢价"直接导向"吸引更多顾客"。
原文 workers who are paid more can spend more 是高工资 → 高消费，选项反成"消费刺激加薪欲望"，因果链方向倒置。
Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness.——作者只是说"暂且搁置"公平这一旧论据，并未说它过时。

questions.stem: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom?
questions.stem_zh: 根据传统观念,提高工资的依据是什么?

options.text: Fairness in distribution.
options.zh: 分配的公平性。

options.text: Increase in productivity.
options.zh: 生产率的提高。

options.text: The priority of economic policymakers.
options.zh: 经济政策制定者的优先事项。

options.text: The unerring judgment of market forces.
options.zh: 市场力量的准确判断。

questions.判型: What is the basis for higher wages according to the conventional wisdom? 用 What 直问按传统观点加薪的依据，回原文找明确陈述句。
questions.拆句: 主句 What is the basis for higher wages + 介词短语 according to the conventional wisdom——according to 引出陈述主体，意味着答案要看 conventional wisdom 那方怎么说，而非作者本人怎么说；六级常借这个介词短语区分立场，须警觉。
questions.定位: P10 The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. 传统观点认为，生产率的提高是通往更高工资的唯一途径。

locate.en: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages.
locate.zh: 传统观点认为，生产率的提高是通往更高工资的唯一途径。

option_analysis.note: Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. 中"公平"是作者列出的另一种加薪理由（且被搁置），与 conventional wisdom 无关。
B 项就是 productivity growth 的同义改写，与预判直接对应。
Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. 是作者本人的主张，不是传统观点对加薪基础的判断。
Mainstream economists insist that ... compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. 是主流经济学家的判断，且原文中"市场力量的无误判断"是指工资水平的决定方式，不是加薪的依据。

questions.stem: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?
questions.stem_zh: 关于美国过去50年左右的现实世界情况,我们了解到什么?

options.text: People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity.
options.zh: 人们未能看到工资和生产率的相应增长。

options.text: People have been disheartened by the widening gap between the haves and have-nots.
options.zh: 人们对贫富差距的扩大感到沮丧。

options.text: People have witnessed a tug of war between Republicans and Democrats over tax cuts.
options.zh: 人们目睹了共和党和民主党就减税问题展开的拉锯战。

options.text: People have seen the link disappearing between productivity and workers' well-being.
options.zh: 人们看到生产率与工人福祉之间的联系正在消失。

questions.判型: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so? 问我们从原文得知的事实，原文必有对应陈述。
questions.拆句: What do we learn about things in the real world in America for the past 50 years or so?——主干是 What do we learn about things，三层介词短语 in the real world/in America/for the past 50 years or so 层层限定 things；六级长题干常用这种层层限定，要逐层抓住主体（things=各种情况）。
questions.定位: P12 In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. 在现实世界里，情况更复杂。工资受到雇主与工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直在胜出。一个明显的证据是，自 1970 年前后以来，生产率增长与工资增长之间的差距越来越大：生产率已经翻了一倍多，而工资远远落在后面。

locate.en: In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
locate.zh: 在现实世界里，情况更复杂。工资受到雇主与工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直在胜出。一个明显的证据是，自 1970 年前后以来，生产率增长与工资增长之间的差距越来越大：生产率已经翻了一倍多，而工资远远落在后面。

option_analysis.note: A 项用 failed to see a corresponding increase 表达"生产率翻倍而工资落后"的整体含义，与预判完全吻合。

pairs.orig: Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
pairs.opt: People have failed to see a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity.

pairs.orig: the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth
pairs.opt: a corresponding increase in wages and in productivity

option_analysis.note: 原文 a tug of war between employers and workers 是劳资博弈，不是贫富分化（haves and have-nots）；且原文未提任何人 disheartened（沮丧）。
原文 a tug of war between employers and workers 是劳资双方的拉锯战，而非两党的争斗；且原文未说民主党与共和党在减税上拉锯。
Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. 说的是"差距扩大"，并未说"联系消失（link disappearing）"——差距大 ≠ 联系断；且 well-being（福祉）也比 wages 范围更大。

reading2.title: 2023年12月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
passages.zh: 期刊编辑决定哪些内容发表、哪些内容不发表，这影响着其他学者的职业生涯，也影响着一个领域的发展方向。因此，人们希望期刊能够竭尽所能建立多元化的编辑委员会，体现各种不同的声音、经历和身份。

passages.en: Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.
passages.zh: 遗憾的是，《自然·神经科学》发表的一项新研究读来令人沮丧。研究团队发现，顶尖心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑都是男性，且任职于美国：这种情况可能正在加剧该领域现有的性别不平等，并影响哪些类型的研究能够发表。

passages.en: Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
passages.zh: 研究发现，男性占心理学期刊编辑的60%。在每个资历级别中，男性编辑人数都显著多于女性编辑，而且在超过四分之三的期刊中，男性占编辑的多数。至关重要的是，女性编辑所占比例显著低于女性心理学研究人员的总体比例。

passages.en: The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.
passages.zh: 神经科学期刊中的差异更加明显：70%的编辑是男性，男性在88%的期刊中占据了多数编辑职位。在这种情况下，女性编辑所占比例并未显著低于从事神经科学研究的女性研究人员所占比例——这一发现揭示了该领域更广泛且持续存在的性别差异。

passages.en: Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience."
passages.zh: 根据研究结果，研究团队得出结论：“在心理学和神经科学领域最受认可的学术期刊编辑职位中，男性的思想、价值观和决策偏见所占比重过大。”

passages.en: Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.
passages.zh: 科学界的性别不平等常常被归因于资深学者更有可能是男性，因为从历史上看，科学一直由男性主导：人们认为，随着时间推移，越来越多的女性晋升到高级职位，这一领域将变得更加平等。然而，这项研究表明，心理学期刊中的初级职位往往也由男性不成比例地担任，尽管事实上，初级心理学教师中女性人数多于男性。

passages.en: This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.
passages.zh: 这意味着，女性学者数量不足并不是问题所在。相反，科学界存在使女性处于不利地位的结构性原因。例如，女性的薪资较低，还要承担更多的育儿责任，这可能导致她们发表的论文和获得的资助更少，而这些正是期刊在决定任命谁时所看重的因素。我们不应仅仅把编辑委员会的不平等归咎于传统，而应积极消除这些现存的障碍。

passages.en: A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.
passages.zh: 期刊编辑缺乏多样性也很可能助长了心理学的WEIRD问题。如果期刊编辑主要是来自美国的男性，那么无论是有意还是无意，他们很可能会更加重视那些与西方男性群体相关的论文。

questions.stem: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities?
questions.stem_zh: 鉴于学术期刊编委会的重要职责,我们期望它展现出什么?

options.text: Insight.
options.zh: 洞察力。

options.text: Expertise.
options.zh: 专业知识。

options.text: Integrity.
options.zh: 诚信。

options.text: Diversity.
options.zh: 多样性。

questions.判型: What would we expect an editorial board of an academic journal to exhibit in view of its important responsibilities? 问的是「鉴于职责，应当呈现什么」，是原文一句话可以直接回答的事实，不含 infer/imply。
questions.拆句: 题干主干是 What would we expect an editorial board…to exhibit，what 作 exhibit 的宾语前置；in view of its important responsibilities 是介词短语作原因状语，可剥离。剥离后等价于 We expect an editorial board to exhibit what?，结构平铺，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. 那么，你会希望期刊竭尽所能去建立一个多元化的编委会，从而反映各种各样的声音、经验与身份。

locate.en: You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
locate.zh: 那么，你会希望期刊竭尽所能去建立一个多元化的编委会，从而反映各种各样的声音、经验与身份。

option_analysis.note: 全文没有任何句子提到「洞察力」相关概念，Insight 是从职责一词主观联想出来的属性。
原文谈的是编辑的「身份多样性」而非「专业能力」；编辑工作虽要求专业，但全文没有任何一句强调专业能力，Expertise 是属性偷换。
全文未出现「诚信／正直」相关讨论，Integrity 同样是从「重要职责」一词联想出的主观属性。
预判语义「多元」与 Diversity 完全同义，其它三项均无对应原文支撑，锁定 D。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience?
questions.stem_zh: 我们从Nature Neuroscience上一项新研究的发现中了解到什么?

options.text: The majority of top psychology and neuroscience journals reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities.
options.zh: 大多数顶级心理学和神经科学期刊反映了多样化的声音、经历和身份。

options.text: The editorial boards of most psychology and neuroscience journals do influence the direction their field takes.
options.zh: 大多数心理学和神经科学期刊的编委会确实影响着其领域发展的方向。

options.text: The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated.
options.zh: 心理学和神经科学领域最重要期刊的编委会由男性主导。

options.text: The majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals have relevant backgrounds.
options.zh: 顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑具有相关背景。

questions.判型: What do we learn from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience? 问的是研究本身陈述了什么，原文有直陈句，不需要跨段推断。
questions.拆句: 题干主干 What do we learn from the findings…?，what 作 learn 的宾语前置；from the findings of a new study in Nature Neuroscience 是 of 套 of 的多层介词结构，但只是限定 findings 来源，对理解无障碍。
questions.定位: P2 The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published. 研究团队发现，顶级心理学与神经科学期刊的大多数编辑是男性，且在美国工作——这种状况可能正在放大该领域既有的性别不平等，并影响着哪些研究得以发表。

locate.en: The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.
locate.zh: 研究团队发现，顶级心理学与神经科学期刊的大多数编辑是男性，且在美国工作——这种状况可能正在放大该领域既有的性别不平等，并影响着哪些研究得以发表。

option_analysis.note: reflect a variety of voices, experiences and identities 是 P1 中作者「期望」的状态，而 P2 恰恰指出现实并非如此——选项把「期待」当成「现实」，方向完全反了。
do influence the direction their field takes 借用 influencing the direction that a field takes，但那是 P1 描述「编辑职责」的总论，不是 P2 的「研究发现」；题干问 findings of a new study，本选项答的是 P1 的背景，与 52 题问的范围错位。
「顶级=最重要」「以男为主=男性主导」两组同义替换都成立，C 是定位句的精确同义复述。

pairs.orig: the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male
pairs.opt: The editorial boards of the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience are male-dominated.
the most important journals in psychology and neuroscience

option_analysis.note: 全文没有任何句子谈及编辑的「相关背景／资质」是否充足；P2 谈的是性别和国籍分布，不是专业相关性，have relevant backgrounds 凭空冒出。

questions.stem: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals?
questions.stem_zh: 关于心理学期刊编辑的性别差异,作者强调了什么事实?

options.text: There were quite a few female editors who also distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers.
options.zh: 有相当多的女性编辑也作为有影响力的心理学研究者脱颖而出。

options.text: The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research.
options.zh: 女性编辑的数量与从事心理学研究的女性数量根本不成比例。

options.text: The proportion of female editors was increasingly lower at senior levels.
options.zh: 女性编辑的比例在高级职位上越来越低。

options.text: There were few female editors who could move up to senior positions.
options.zh: 很少有女性编辑能够晋升到高级职位。

questions.判型: What fact does the author highlight concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals? 问的是「作者强调了什么事实」，原文有一句直接陈述，属细节而非主旨。
questions.拆句: 题干主干 What fact does the author highlight…?；concerning the gender differences in editors of psychology journals 是 concerning 引导的介词短语作 highlight 的范围状语，限定话题。结构平铺，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers. 至关重要的是，女性编辑的占比显著低于心理学领域整体女性研究者的占比。

locate.en: Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
locate.zh: 至关重要的是，女性编辑的占比显著低于心理学领域整体女性研究者的占比。

option_analysis.note: 原文只对比「女编辑占比」与「女研究者占比」，并未说有「兼任出色研究者的女编辑」；distinguished themselves as influential psychology researchers 是凭空添加的属性。
唯一刻画「女编辑占比 vs 女研究者占比」这一比例对照的选项是 B；其它选项要么换了对比对象，要么换了讨论范围。

pairs.orig: the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers
pairs.opt: The number of female editors was simply disproportionate to that of women engaged in psychology research.

pairs.orig: the overall proportion of women psychology researchers
pairs.opt: that of women engaged in psychology research

options.text: Women's views are underrepresented in the editorial boards of top psychology and neuroscience journals.
options.zh: 女性的观点在顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的编委会中代表性不足。

options.text: Male editors of top psychology and neuroscience journals tend to be biased against their female colleagues.
options.zh: 顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的男性编辑往往对其女性同事存在偏见。

options.text: Male researchers have enough representation in the editorial boards to ensure their publications.

options.text: Female editors have to struggle to get women's research articles published in academic journals.

questions.判型: What can we infer from the conclusion drawn by the team of the new study on the basis of their findings? 含明确的 infer 标志词，正确答案是定位句的一步同义延伸，而非原文逐字表述。
questions.拆句: 题干主干 What can we infer from the conclusion…?；drawn by the team of the new study 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 conclusion；on the basis of their findings 是介词短语状语，说明结论的依据。三层修饰仅在定位 conclusion 这个核心名词，不影响主干理解，但基础薄弱的同学要看清 from 后面真正的对象是 conclusion 而不是 team。
questions.定位: P5 Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience." 基于研究结果，研究团队总结道：「在最受认可的心理学与神经科学学术期刊的编辑岗位上，男性的想法、价值观与决策偏见被过度代表。」

locate.en: Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience."
locate.zh: 基于研究结果，研究团队总结道：「在最受认可的心理学与神经科学学术期刊的编辑岗位上，男性的想法、价值观与决策偏见被过度代表。」

option_analysis.note: 在「男过度代表」基础上仅走一步就到「女代表不足」，A 是唯一这样做的；其它选项要么走第二步（偏见、歧视），要么换了话题。

原文从未谈论女编辑为发表女性研究而「斗争」，struggle to get women's research articles published 是凭空虚构出来的情节。

questions.stem: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition?
questions.stem_zh: 作者建议我们做什么,而不是简单地将编委会的不平等归咎于传统?

options.text: Strike a balance between male and female editors.
options.zh: 在男性和女性编辑之间取得平衡。

options.text: Increase women's employment in senior positions.
options.zh: 增加女性在高级职位上的任职。

options.text: Enlarge the body of female academics.
options.zh: 扩大女性学者的群体。

options.text: Implement overall structural reforms.
options.zh: 实施全面的结构性改革。

questions.判型: What does the author suggest we do instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition? 问作者明确建议什么，原文有 Rather than… we should… 的直陈句，是细节题而非主旨题。
questions.拆句: 题干主干 What does the author suggest we do，what 作 do 的宾语前置；instead of simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition 是 instead of 引导的动名词介词短语，作状语，表达「与其…不如…」的对比关系。看清 instead of 后面是「要被否定的旧做法」，suggest we do 后面才是「要肯定的新做法」，二者不可弄反。
questions.定位: P7 Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers. 实际上，是结构性的原因让女性在科学界处于不利地位。例如，女性薪资更低、育儿负担更重，这会导致她们论文与基金更少——而这些恰恰是期刊在选拔编辑时所看重的。与其简单地把编委会的不平等推给传统，不如主动去拆除这些既有的壁垒。

locate.en: Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.
locate.zh: 实际上，是结构性的原因让女性在科学界处于不利地位。例如，女性薪资更低、育儿负担更重，这会导致她们论文与基金更少——而这些恰恰是期刊在选拔编辑时所看重的。与其简单地把编委会的不平等推给传统，不如主动去拆除这些既有的壁垒。

option_analysis.note: Strike a balance between male and female editors 只触及「编辑性别比例」这一表层结果，与作者主张的「拆除导致不平等的结构性原因」相比，停留在症状而非根因；原文反对的就是「只盯比例不动结构」的浅层对策。
Increase women's employment in senior positions 借的是 P6 「初级岗位也男性偏多」这一对照性数据；但 P6 是作者用来「驳斥传统论」的论据，并非建议；55 题问的是「P7 作者建议什么」。
原文 This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. 已明确否定「女学者太少」是问题；Enlarge the body of female academics 恰恰反过来主张「扩充女学者队伍」，方向完全相反。
把「主动拆除结构性壁垒」概括为「实施整体结构性改革」，是 D 与原文唯一吻合的同义改写；其它选项要么停留在「男女比例」「升迁」等局部对策，要么误把原因当对策。

structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science

translation.title: 2023年12月·第1套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍中国养老模式现状与展望 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 在中国，随着老龄化社会的到来，养老受到普遍关注。人们谈论最多的是应当采取什么样的养老模式。多数人认为，养老模式需要多元化。可以通过政府引导和社会参与，建立更多更好的养老服务机构，改进社区服务中心，鼓励居家自助养老，还可以推行家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式。随着政府和社会对养老服务事业投入的持续增加，养老设施将不断升级，服务质量逐步改进，老年人的生活将会更加方便舒适、健康快乐。
translation.reference_en:
In China, with the arrival of an aging society, elderly care has drawn widespread attention. What people talk about most is what model of elderly care should be adopted. Most people believe that the elderly-care model needs to be diversified. To achieve this, through governmental guidance and social participation, we can build more and better elderly-care institutions, improve community service centers, encourage self-supported home-based elderly care, and promote a combination of family-based and society-based elderly care. With the continuous increase in government and social investment in elderly-care services, elderly-care facilities will be steadily upgraded, service quality will gradually improve, and the elderly will live a more convenient, comfortable, healthy and happy life.
【衔接】
